name: angle-estimator
title: Angle estimator
tagline: One angle from two rays at an authored size, for estimating by eye and classifying (acute/right/obtuse/reflex/straight); size and type derived, reading occludable, guides optional.
description: Two rays from a common vertex draw a single angle at the size you author, for building angle sense WITHOUT a protractor: estimate the angle by eye and classify it. You write only the angle's size in degrees (and optionally how the whole figure is rotated); the model draws the two arms and the arc between them, derives the reading, and derives the classification — acute (< 90), right (= 90, drawn as a square not an arc), obtuse (90–180), straight (= 180), or reflex (> 180, the arc sweeping the long way round). There is nowhere to author the reading or the type, so a 127° angle always reads 127° and always classifies as obtuse. Occlude the reading (it shows "?") for "estimate this angle" or "is this acute or obtuse?"; reveal it to check. Turn on faint benchmark guides (a right-angle marker at 90°, a straight-line marker at 180°) as an estimation scaffold. Highlight the angle, name it (∠ABC, x°), or show the arm-point letters for the three-letter naming convention. v1 draws exactly one angle per figure as a static stimulus — classifying or estimating is answered in the question block's text, not on the figure.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever the lesson is angle SENSE by eye rather than measuring with an instrument: estimate the size of an angle, classify an angle as acute / right / obtuse / reflex / straight, compare an angle against the benchmark angles 45 / 90 / 180, and the three-letter angle-naming convention ∠ABC. Author only `size` (the angle in degrees) and optionally `rotate` (turn the whole figure so the angle is not always sitting on the horizontal — good practice, since real angles are not axis-aligned). Common configurations: a worked labelled example — `size` with the reading and the derived type shown; an "estimate this angle" question — set `occlude: true` so the reading shows "?" (the type is hidden too so nothing leaks), optionally with `guides: ["right-angle"]` so pupils have 90° to judge against; a "classify this angle" set — several blocks at different sizes with `show.reading: false` and `show.type: false`, asking acute/obtuse/reflex; a hard discrimination pair — 88° and 92° with the right-angle guide, so pupils must decide just-acute vs just-obtuse. For the naming convention set `armLabels` to the three point letters (vertex letter shown in the middle of ∠ABC). A reflex angle is just `size` over 180 — the arc sweeps the long way and the type reads "reflex"; do not use a protractor's subtract-from-360 method here (that is geometry/protractor). Keep `rotate` and the show-flags consistent across the blocks of one lesson so pupils compare like with like. Switch primitive when the teaching changes: to lay a graduated instrument on the angle and read the scale use geometry/protractor; for angle facts at a point (vertically opposite, angles on a line, angle sums, forming equations) use geometry/angles-at-a-point; for a fraction of a full turn (quarter / half / three-quarter turn, clockwise) use geometry/turn or geometry/clock. Synonyms a teacher might use: estimate an angle, guess the angle, angle sense, classify angles, name the angle, acute, right angle, obtuse, reflex, straight angle, types of angle, benchmark angles, without a protractor, ∠ABC naming.

size.description: The angle in DEGREES between the two rays (0 to 360, exclusive). This is the ONE semantic input: the arm directions, the arc, the reading and the classification are all derived from it. Under 90 is acute; exactly 90 is a right angle (drawn as a square); over 90 to under 180 is obtuse; exactly 180 is a straight angle; over 180 is reflex (the arc sweeps the long way round). Whole degrees read most naturally.

rotate.description: Rotate the WHOLE figure, in degrees anticlockwise from east: the first (baseline) arm points along `rotate`, the second arm at `rotate + size`. 0 sits the baseline arm horizontally to the right. Tilt it (e.g. 20, 155) so the angle is not always axis-aligned — pupils should judge an angle in any orientation, not just off the horizontal. Default 0.

label.description: Name shown beside the arc instead of the derived reading — e.g. "∠ABC", "x°", or "a". Omit to show the derived reading ("127°"). An occluded angle shows "?" regardless of this.

occlude.description: Hide the answer: the reading shows "?" AND the derived type is suppressed (nothing leaks in the figure or the aria-label) — the "estimate this angle / is it acute or obtuse?" hook. The angle itself stays drawn. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to this angle — its arc and reading go amber (the result / emphasis colour). Default false.

armLabels.description: Three point letters for the three-letter naming convention: [firstArmTip, vertex, secondArmTip], e.g. ["A","B","C"] draws A at the first arm's end, B at the vertex, C at the second arm's end — so the angle is read ∠ABC (vertex in the middle). Omit for an unlabelled angle.

guides.description: Faint benchmark markers to judge against, drawn in construction grey from the baseline arm: "right-angle" adds a 90° guide ray with a small square, "straight" adds a 180° guide ray along the straight line. A scaffold for estimation ("is it more or less than a right angle?"). Their directions are derived from `rotate`. Omit for none.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional sentence centred below the figure: a stem sentence ("The angle is about ___ degrees"). Rendered in a warm band. An occluded value referenced here should be written as "?" by the author. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

reading.description: Show the derived reading (e.g. "127°") beside the arc. false hides the number (a pure classify / estimate figure). Per-angle occlude shows "?" instead. Default true.

type.description: Show the derived classification word (acute / right angle / obtuse / straight / reflex) below the reading. false hides it so pupils name it themselves. Auto-hidden when occluded. Default true.

arc.description: Draw the arc (or right-angle square) between the two arms. false leaves just the two bare rays. Default true.
